metaDescription: Odoo has no BOQ, no retention and no progress billing. How a contractor build is actually assembled, what breaks, and the country rules that change it.
intro: There is no construction app in Odoo. Nothing in 17, 18 or 19 holds a bill of quantities, a payment certificate, a retention balance or a variation register. A contracting system is assembled from parts that do exist: the site as a project and an analytic account, the BOQ as priced order lines, valuation as delivered quantity, and each subcontract as a purchase order with its own budget.

The build earns its keep on committed cost. A contractor already knows what has been spent, because the ledger says so. What kills a job is what has been ordered and not yet invoiced. Purchase orders raised against a site carry an analytic distribution, so committed value sits beside actual and budget on one report, and a package that has blown its allowance shows in week six rather than at handover.

Community covers more than buyers expect: Project, Timesheets, analytic plans and distribution models, Sales, Purchase agreements, multi step stock transfers, landed costs, Maintenance and Fleet. Enterprise buys the Gantt view, Planning, Field Service, Documents, Sign, Approvals, Studio, Payroll and the localised e-invoicing and tax filing modules. Retention, BOQ import and a payment certificate layout are in neither edition, and each one is a line in the budget.
whoFor: Main contractors and subcontractors on fixed price work, where the cost of a site has to land on the job rather than on the company.
Developers who need land, construction and finance cost to accumulate against a plot before a single unit is handed over.
MEP, civils and fit out specialists billing measured work and carrying retention across a defects liability period.
Contracting arms inside a group already running Odoo, still raising interim applications in a spreadsheet outside the ledger.
Not for a two person jobbing builder, where Project and Invoicing alone do the work and a cost coding structure is overhead nobody will maintain.
Not for design workflow: Odoo holds no drawings, no model geometry and no clash detection, and it will not replace what your engineers draw in.

capabilities.title: The site as a project and an analytic account
capabilities.body: Every site gets a project for the work and an analytic account for the money. A second analytic plan holds the cost code or work package, a third the funding source on joint venture and government jobs. One journal item splits across all of them by percentage. Analytic distribution models apply that split from the partner, the product or the project automatically, which is what stops site staff having to type it.

capabilities.title: Bills of quantity as priced order lines
capabilities.body: A BOQ imports as order lines with a section per element, a quantity, a unit and a rate. Odoo has no measurement sheet, so the take off stays in the estimator's spreadsheet and the priced summary comes across. Set the line to invoice on delivered quantity entered manually, and the delivered figure becomes this month's measured work. Provisional sums stay as separate lines so they can move without touching priced work.

capabilities.title: Interim valuations and payment certificates
capabilities.body: Billing runs on delivered quantity. The quantity surveyor updates the measured amount per line, the invoice picks up the difference, and cumulative certified value sits on the order instead of in a parallel file. Odoo prints an invoice, not a certificate in the format an employer signs, so that layout is a report you commission. Advances use the standard down payment invoice with a recovery line on later applications.

capabilities.title: Retention as accounts, not as a field
capabilities.body: There is no retention field. The pattern that works is a retention line on the invoice at the contract percentage, posted to a retention receivable account rather than to trade debtors, so the balance sheet separates money held from money overdue. Release is a separate invoice at practical completion and again at the end of the defects period. The mirror treatment applies to retention held from subcontractors.

capabilities.title: Subcontract packages, not manufacturing subcontracting
capabilities.body: The subcontracting feature in Odoo belongs to Manufacturing and means sending components to a vendor to be made into something. It is not a civils package. A subcontract is a purchase order against the site with its own budget, valued as work is certified, with back charges, retention and materials issued to the trade netted off the payment. Purchase agreements hold the rates let for the package.

capabilities.title: Plant, materials and what is still an asset
capabilities.body: Owned plant sits in Fleet or Maintenance with readings and a service history, and internal hire posts to the site at an agreed rate. Material bought for a site is a transfer to a site location, not a cost, so unfixed material on site remains stock the company owns. Landed costs push freight, clearance and offloading onto the receipt, which matters where steel and cladding arrive by container.

setup.title: Agree the cost code structure first
setup.body: The cost breakdown decides every report the business will run, and it is not a setting you revisit. Two analytic plans are easy to live with, one for the site and one for the work package. Five become an entry burden that site staff quietly skip. Keep the code list short enough for a foreman to pick from on a phone. Retro-fitting coding across a year of posted entries is manual work nobody budgets for.

setup.title: Load open contracts at one cutover date
setup.body: There is no clean way to import a job that is half built. Take each live contract at a single date with contract value, approved variations, value certified, amounts invoiced, retention held and cost to date as an opening analytic balance. Reconcile that against the last certificate the employer signed before anything is posted. Replaying two years of interim applications into Odoo has no upside.

setup.title: Decide how labour reaches the job
setup.body: Labour decides whether a job made money and it is the hardest cost to collect. Timesheets in Community are a form, which office staff will use and a steel fixer will not. The realistic options are a daily allocation keyed by a site clerk, a card or biometric reader feeding attendance, or the Enterprise timesheet grid for supervisors. Pick one and fund it, because a project with no labour cost is a report nobody believes.

setup.title: Treat variations as their own documents
setup.body: A variation is not an edit to the original order. Raise it with its own reference, its own approval and its own status, so contract value reads as original plus approved variations plus instructions still pending. Pending work has to be visible before it is approved, because that is the number a commercial manager argues from. Merging variations into the original order destroys the trail the employer will eventually ask to see.

setup.title: Fix the retention and work in progress accounts with the accountant
setup.body: Retention receivable, retention payable, work in progress and the account carrying uncertified cost are agreed during design. Odoo has no percentage of completion engine, so revenue recognised over time is a monthly journal built from the analytic report, and somebody has to own it. Settling this early avoids the conversation where an auditor asks how work in progress was derived and the honest answer is a spreadsheet.

pitfalls.title: One analytic account called Head Office
pitfalls.body: The fastest configuration puts every cost on a single account and removes the reason for doing the project. Cost per site, per package and per trade collapse into the number the owner already had. It usually happens because purchase orders are raised by an office that does not know the site code. The fix is a default distribution on the vendor and the product category, plus a rule that an uncoded order is not approved.

pitfalls.title: Committed cost ignored until the bill arrives
pitfalls.body: A contractor reading only posted cost is several weeks late. An order is a commitment the moment it is issued, and the exposure on a package is ordered value, not invoiced value. Odoo can show it, because purchase order lines carry the analytic distribution, but the report has to be asked for. Without it, a package that has already spent its allowance stays green until the vendor invoices.

pitfalls.title: Materials expensed the day they are bought
pitfalls.body: Booking steel, block and cable straight to cost when the vendor bill posts makes early months look expensive and late months look profitable, and job margin is wrong all the way through. Material bought for a site is stock until it is fixed. Receive it into a site location, issue it against the work, and accept the extra transaction rather than a monthly count nobody has time to do.

pitfalls.title: Retention forgotten until somebody asks
pitfalls.body: Retention released two years late is the most common piece of free money left on the table in this industry. If the balance sits inside trade debtors, nobody can separate an overdue invoice from money contractually held, and the collections report becomes noise. Put it in its own account, hold the release dates as activities on the contract, and give one person the job of chasing them.

pitfalls.title: Site staff asked to work like office staff
pitfalls.body: Rollouts fail on the site, not in the finance office. A foreman with a phone in a dusty pocket will not complete a form with fourteen required fields. Cut the site facing screens to what somebody can finish standing up, use the mobile views rather than the desktop form, and let the office correct coding afterwards. No amount of reporting configuration fixes an adoption problem.

worksWith: Project and Timesheets, for the programme, the task structure and labour cost against a site
Accounting, for analytic distribution, retention accounts, landed costs and the month end accrual
Purchase, with agreements holding the rates let for a package before it is awarded
Inventory, with a stock location per site so unfixed material stays an asset rather than a cost
Sales, where the BOQ lives as priced lines and applications invoice from delivered quantity
Maintenance and Fleet, so plant hours, servicing and fuel post against the site that used them
Field Service, Documents, Sign and Approvals in Enterprise, for snagging, drawing storage, signed instructions and authority limits
HR and Payroll, for accommodation cost, gratuity accrual and the wage file the local regime requires

regional.note: ZATCA Phase 2 clears every standard invoice through Fatoora before it reaches the employer, so an interim application cannot be issued until the measured figure is agreed. Odoo Enterprise carries the Saudi e-invoicing integration and Community does not. VAT is 15 percent, site labour is paid through WPS, and Saudization quotas make the trade mix a compliance question as well as a cost.

The VAT point on a progress payment is the earliest of the invoice, the payment received, or twelve months after the work was done, so retention held for years still triggers tax eventually. Corporate tax at 9 percent applies above the threshold, e-invoicing is moving to a Peppol based model on a phased timetable, and site labour is paid through WPS.

Final payments to a contractor are commonly held against a tax clearance from the General Tax Authority, so retention release depends on a certificate arriving on the authority's timetable rather than yours. Filing runs through Dhareeba, there is no VAT yet, withholding applies on payments to non-residents, and wages go through the Wage Protection System.

FBR digital invoicing pushes sales tax invoices to the board as they are raised, while sales tax on construction services is provincial, so a contractor working in Sindh and Punjab files with SRB and PRA under different rules. Income tax is withheld at source on contract payments, and every deduction certificate has to be matched to the client's payment before it can be claimed.

A works contract is a supply of service at 18 percent GST, and input tax credit on construction of immovable property is blocked, so material tax becomes cost rather than credit and the estimate has to be built that way. Running account bills follow measurement, e-invoicing applies above the turnover threshold, and every delivery of material to site needs an e-way bill.

Under the domestic reverse charge a subcontractor invoices without VAT and the contractor accounts for it, which changes both the invoice layout and the return. CIS deducts twenty or thirty percent from the labour element of every subcontractor payment, with a monthly return, and none of that exists in standard Odoo. Making Tax Digital also requires digital links from record to submission.

Bauabzugsteuer withholds fifteen percent from payments to a construction subcontractor unless a valid exemption certificate is on file, so its expiry date belongs on the vendor record. Construction services between contractors fall under the section 13b reverse charge and carry no VAT. GoBD demands records that cannot be altered after posting, and the accountant will expect a DATEV export.

Progress claims run under security of payment legislation, where a payment schedule has to be issued inside a statutory window or the claimed amount becomes payable, which makes certification a hard deadline rather than a target. Retention on larger projects may have to sit in a trust account, payments to subcontractors are reported annually through the taxable payments report, and GST is claimed on the BAS.

faqs.q: Does Odoo have a construction or contracting module?
faqs.a: No. Odoo 17, 18 and 19 hold no bill of quantities, no payment certificate, no retention balance, no variation register and no drawing control. What exists are the parts a contracting system is built from: projects, analytic plans, sales and purchase documents, inventory and timesheets. Anything advertised as an Odoo construction module is third party or bespoke, and should be assessed as code you will end up maintaining.

faqs.q: Can we run this on Odoo Community?
faqs.a: Most of it. Projects, timesheets, analytic plans and distribution models, purchase agreements, multi step transfers, landed costs, Maintenance and Fleet are all Community. Enterprise buys the Gantt view, Planning, Field Service, Documents, Sign, Approvals, Studio, Payroll and the localised e-invoicing modules. If you invoice under a clearance regime such as ZATCA Phase 2, that last item usually decides the edition.

faqs.q: How does progress billing work without a progress billing feature?
faqs.a: The order line carries the contract quantity and the delivered quantity carries what has been measured. The surveyor updates the measured figure, the invoice picks up the difference, and cumulative certified value sits on the order. What Odoo will not do is print a payment certificate in the format an employer signs, so that report is commissioned as part of the build.

Not as a field. It is a retention line on the invoice posting to its own receivable account, with the release raised as a separate invoice at practical completion and again at the end of the defects period. The mirror treatment applies to retention held from subcontractors. It is a configuration and reporting exercise, and it takes an afternoon to agree with your accountant.

faqs.q: Will Odoo replace our BIM or design software?
faqs.a: No. Odoo holds no drawings, no model geometry, no CAD revisions and no clash detection. Documents in Enterprise stores files against a project with versioning, which covers issued for construction drawings and transmittals as records. The model stays where your engineers draw it, and the sensible link is a shared reference number rather than an attempt to merge the two.

faqs.q: How do we cost a subcontractor who also takes our materials?
faqs.a: Materials issued to a trade are a stock movement against that subcontractor rather than a sale, valued at cost and netted against certified value on the payment. Back charges for rectification, plant hire and site services work the same way. The order carries the agreed rates, and the gap between ordered, certified and paid is the number to report weekly.

faqs.q: How long does a construction rollout take?
faqs.a: Configuration is measured in weeks. The date is set by whether cost codes exist anywhere other than in the commercial manager's head, and whether site staff will record labour and material against a job. One company with a few live contracts and clean opening balances moves quickly. A group with joint ventures and two years of open final accounts is a different project.
